title: Harvest readiness and harvest workflow — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define an evidence-led cannabis harvest workflow that separates maturity assessment from sanitation, lot identity, authorization, segregation and transfer into postharvest control.

excludedUntilValidated: one universal number of flowering weeks
harvest decision from one convenience flower
release of suspect or contaminated material because maturity appears acceptable

claims.statement: Cannabinoid concentration and other inflorescence characteristics change during flowering and harvest timing can materially affect the chemical profile and yield objective.
claims.boundary: The timing of peak concentration varies by genotype and production context, so one calendar week cannot be used as a universal harvest rule.

claims.statement: Stigma color transition can provide a useful maturity approximation for many cannabis genotypes, but some genotypes reach cannabinoid peaks at earlier color stages.
claims.boundary: A mostly-amber rule of thumb is not a substitute for genotype-specific validation or the defined product objective.

claims.statement: Glandular trichome development and senescence are influenced by plant age and genotype, and different trichomes on the same inflorescence can be at different developmental stages.
claims.boundary: A single trichome image or color count cannot prove whole-lot maturity or exact cannabinoid concentration.

claims.statement: Trichome browning and structural senescence can accompany maturation, while stress and postharvest handling can also affect trichome appearance, so visual observations require crop and handling context.
claims.boundary: Visual color alone should not be treated as a direct laboratory measurement of cannabinoid content.

claims.statement: Representative maturity sampling should preserve plant/zone position, date, genotype, crop stage, sampled tissue and observation method so repeated checks and harvest decisions remain comparable.
claims.boundary: Convenience sampling from the most visually mature top flower can overstate lot readiness.

claims.statement: Harvest execution should preserve lot identity, tool/equipment sanitation status, affected crop scope, cut/trim location and transfer history so later drying, testing and deviations can be traced back to the source material.
claims.boundary: A mature crop is not automatically releasable if identity, sanitation, contamination or quality status is unresolved.

claims.statement: Material from different rooms, zones, genotypes or materially different process histories should not be combined in a way that destroys the ability to reconstruct their source and exposure history.
claims.boundary: Facility lot-definition rules can differ, but traceability should remain sufficient for investigation and disposition.

claims.statement: The harvest-to-drying handoff should communicate exact lot identity, harvest timing, observed maturity evidence, deviations/holds, sanitary status and required next processing step.
claims.boundary: Handoff documentation does not clear an existing contamination, testing or quality hold.
